# Zelenskyy accuses Russia of escalating strikes ahead of peace talks
By Al Jazeera Staff, AFP, AP and Reuters

(Fetch tool returned a condensed rendering; text below is as returned.)

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has accused Russia of intensifying strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure to pressure Kyiv ahead of upcoming talks.

Moscow's strikes come as temperatures drop in Ukraine, days before US-brokered talks are set to take place in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday to revive stalled diplomatic efforts.

"By intensifying its attacks on Ukraine and our infrastructure at this very moment, Russia is trying to additionally lay the groundwork for putting pressure on Ukraine's position and that of its partners," Zelenskyy stated on Saturday.

"The capital is facing serious difficulties with its electricity, water, and heat supplies," Zelenskyy added, noting that substations were also hit in five regions.

He reported that Russia had launched 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles, including North Korean-manufactured KN-23 missiles. Ukraine managed to intercept only four of the 36 missiles.

Zelenskyy urged increased U.S. support, stating: "Unfortunately, there is still a significant shortage of interceptors for Patriot systems, and the United States is in the best position to help address it."

The attacks killed at least two people across Ukraine and wounded approximately a dozen others, according to authorities. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko reported that overnight strikes damaged energy facilities and a key bridge in the capital, describing the energy situation as "extremely difficult."

The attacks occurred days before US-led talks between Moscow and Kyiv in Abu Dhabi.
